segments.expected: "I'm putting a fourth column on the sheet for tomorrow night," he said to Kiva. "The Board sits at seven, at the Salt Hall, on the Chair's three. I've people, and rifts and spawn, and Saltmere. I'm adding ash." He touched the ledger on the desk's ledge. "What the comb says. How much of every year's yield sang on the seventh. It goes up with the others. It went up faster from the fifth month, the same as the others." He looked at her. "I'll draw the four on one sheet with one rule along the bottom for the weeks. I'll not draw anything between them. If the Board wants a line, it'll have to draw it itself."

segments.expected: "They look at the girl with three doors. That's different. That's a thing you can do." He breathed carefully. "This is a thing you are. They'll look at you as though you'd been sent for. I know you. You'd hate that worse than anything." He paused. "I'm not saying don't. I'm the captain, and it's not a captain's to say. I'm saying I know what it'll cost you, and I'll be on the hurdle with my hands in my pockets when they look."
